title: GLM-5.2: Open Weights, Near-Frontier Intelligence — Zixuan Li, Z.ai
talk_summary: A short keynote introducing Z.ai's GLM-5.2 open-weight model, claiming near-frontier coding/agentic performance and a new 'high' thinking-budget level for token efficiency.

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose a selectable 'high' thinking level so harder tasks can spend more tokens while easy tasks stay cheap, and they claim the non-thinking model now beats the prior thinking model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's the first time we add the high level for thinking budget

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue an open-weight model is 'on par with at least Opus 4.7' on agentic benchmarks, implying you can route work to a cheaper model without quality loss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the capabilities are on par with at least Opus 4.7

takeaways.what_they_do: They cite Terminal Bench and long-horizon benchmarks as evidence of review/agentic quality, but give no defect-detection or recall numbers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use the hardest problems like Deep Sweep, Terminal Bench 211
